name: PR Review
instructions:
You are a review assistant. Your job is to post the review on the PR with a given format.

IMPORTANT: Do not Approve/Request Changes/ Merge Without Approval.

On start: call hive_set_context with pr (GitHub URL), jira (issue key), branch (git branch), and either plan (absolute file path) or planText (markdown summary of your plan). Update context as things change.

1. Deep review the PR
2. Post and Present the information in the following format
a. Author / Title / Link
b. What is the change meant to fix
c. Product Impact - Before and After
d. Flow Diagram with Upstream and Downstream Impact
e. Blast Radius - Extra  Large/ Large  / Medium / Low 
f. Recommendations on lowering the blast radius
g. Risks - Production Risk, Migration Risk, Code Maintainability Risk, Pattern Breaking Risk
h. Final Recommendation

3. Post a comment on the PR
4. Post a slack message to #hive-pr-review (channel ID: C0AJ54FMXM5)

If author=nukulb 
then automatically close hive task by calling hive_complete_task
else Wait for My Approval.

IF not sure then wait for my approval.
memory: When updateEvvData detects that the approved time hasn't actually changed (checkInTimeActuallyChanged=false), it skips manualCheckInOut. But GPS suggestion coords still need to be persisted in this case, requiring an additional $set update.

Data import pipeline: nested array sub-fields (like rate exception times, authorization constraints) bypass buildModelMapper, requiring explicit valueMapperOverrides registered via buildNestedArrayFieldMapperOverrides helper
MongoDB $push operations bypass Mongoose schema enum validation — the import pipeline must validate these constraints (e.g., daysOfWeek 0-6 range) at the application level
Rate panel UI uses date-fns strict hh:mma parser — time strings from CSV must be normalized to canonical hh:mmA format (no spaces, zero-padded hours, uppercase meridiem)

The normalizeTime12h value mapper handles: space before meridiem ('09:00 AM'), no zero-pad ('9:00AM'), lowercase ('9:00 am'), and 24-hour format ('17:00') — returns original string if unparseable so validators can produce meaningful errors
PR review pattern: large PRs that bundle unrelated changes across shared pipeline files (parseCsv.service.js, validation.js) significantly increase blast radius — recommend splitting into focused PRs

Data Import module: IMPORT_FAILED status means zero records were imported (importedRecords: 0). PARTIAL is used when some records were imported. This distinction is confirmed by canDeleteImportSession vs canForceDeleteImportSessionAndRecords in sessionAction.utils.js.

Data Import session status flow: NEW → PARSING → READY/NO_VALID_RECORDS → IMPORTING → COMPLETED/PARTIAL/IMPORT_FAILED. The canResetImportSession function gates which statuses can be reset back to NEW.
ImportMappingPanel.js uses a sessionFinal flag derived from deriveSessionStatusFlags to guard auto-reprocessing in handleResolutionPanelClose. This prevents unintended reparsing from terminal states.
The #hive-pr-review Slack channel either doesn't exist or is a private channel the bot token doesn't have access to. Channel not found when attempting to post via slack-msg.sh.

MongoDB transaction session propagation is a recurring pattern in the data import codebase. The connection handler already had it correct, but caregiver and admin handlers were missing it. When reviewing data import PRs, check all entity handlers for consistent session propagation.
The GitHub MCP tool (mcp__github__*) returns 'Not Found' for the mavencare/webplatform repo - likely an auth issue. Use `gh` CLI as fallback for all GitHub operations.
For PR reviews with backticks/special characters in the body, write to a temp file first and use `gh pr review --body-file` to avoid bash interpolation issues.

In the dataset report builder, grouped views use `dataFormatter` to render inline content in MetaDataTableGroupRowData. The formatter must include the label (e.g., formatDisplayField) because grouped rows show multiple fields inline - unlike table columns where the header is in a separate row.

formatDisplayField is a HOF: formatDisplayField(label) returns ({value}, ref, context) => JSX that renders both label and value. formatDisplayNumberValue only renders the value right-aligned. In grouped contexts, always use the label-bearing formatter.

The _buildGroupedMetadataFieldFromDatasetViewFieldConfig function in dataset.metadata.utils.js handles grouped view field construction separately from the non-grouped view (which starts around line 360). Changes to one do not affect the other.
E11000 duplicate key errors in integration tests are caused by hardcoded unique fields (invoiceNumber, attribute text) — fix by using random/unique values with testId or Math.random()
sinon's positional call assertions (firstCall, fourthCall, getCall(N)) are brittle when the SUT's internal call order can change — prefer getCalls().find() with predicate matching on args
Feature cache leaking between Mocha tests causes flaky behavior — add clearFeatureCache() in beforeEach when tests interact with feature flags

When test functions iterate with `for...of`, a common bug is referencing the array variable (details.rate) instead of the loop variable (detail.price) — always verify singular vs plural variable names in loops
E2E flaky tests often need toPass() retry wrappers for non-retrying assertions and explicit visibility waits between rapid sequential actions (clickApply → wait → clickSave)
Salesforce Lumen is a new CRM integration variant alongside V2/V3, with enhanced mapping, assessment questions, and dual auth (OAuth + Client Credentials)

The integration engine shared modules (salesforce.mapping.utils.js, salesforce.resolution.js, salesforce.api.js) are shared between V2 and Lumen — changes to these are high-risk and should be verified against V2 tests
SOQL injection requires escaping single quotes as '' (two single quotes), not \' — different from SQL
The sqsIntegration config in sharedConfig.defaults.js has a specific shape that other code depends on — changing it requires backward compatibility
PR #27504 has 55 files and 13.6k additions — extra-large blast radius PRs benefit from being split, especially shared module changes

geo.utils.js already has getSelfAndAllDescendantGeoIds() for expanding geo IDs with descendants. New code creating similar helpers should consider reusing it (returns ObjectIds vs strings is the main difference).
Pay group geo filtering uses 3 separate functions (resolveCaregiversForGroup, resolvePayGroupForCaregiver, resolveRosterTargets) — all 3 must be updated together when changing geo matching behavior.
allDescendantGeoIds on the Geo model is maintained by geo.hierarchy.utils.js and is a reliable source for geo hierarchy expansion.

EVV aggregator processAcknowledgmentResults has a 3-step pipeline: Step 1 stores raw response, Step 2 processes per-record results, Step 3 sweeps remaining PENDING messages to REJECTED as a safety net. The isLatest field controls visibility in the admin submissions report.

The admin UI's 'Acknowledge Exception' button is gated by exceptionCode (isRejected && hasExceptionCode), not by isLatest. Setting isLatest: false on swept messages was redundant and caused a worse problem by hiding them entirely from the report.

Swept messages (Step 3) have exceptionMessage but no exceptionCode since SANDATA omits them from per-record results. This naturally hides the 'Acknowledge Exception' button in the UI without needing isLatest: false.

Existing swept messages with isLatest: false already in the DB will remain hidden after this fix. Only newly swept messages will be visible. A one-time DB update would be needed to surface historical swept messages.

EVV aggregator entity correction flow: holdVisitsForEntityCorrection (DEV-44205) targets unsent PENDING visits (sandataTransactionId === null). New supersedeInFlightVisitsForEntityCorrection (DEV-44371) targets already-submitted visits (sandataTransactionId !== null). Together they cover all visit states.

The waitingFor.clientId and waitingFor.caregiverId fields are always populated on visit messages by queueVisitWithDependencies() upsert, so querying by these fields on PENDING messages with sandataTransactionId is safe.

requeueHeldVisits reuses queueVisit() which triggers queueVisitWithDependencies upsert - this naturally keeps messages in WAITING_FOR_DEPENDENCIES because the entity correction hasn't been acknowledged yet.

Code duplication pattern: client and caregiver changestream listeners have near-identical requeueHeldVisits implementations (~130 lines each). This is a known pattern in the EVV aggregator codebase where client/caregiver logic is mirrored.
REQUIRES_EVV_CHANGE_REASON model config return shape changed from boolean to {required, onlyForSubmittedChanges} in PR #27472 - all consumers must use ?.required ?? config pattern
doChangesRequireAnEvvChangeReason had a bug where moment(undefined).isSame(moment(undefined)) returns false - now uses areDatesEqual for all date comparisons
New API endpoint GET /bookings/:id/requires-evv-change-reason checks AggregatorOutboxMessage to determine if visit was submitted to aggregator
New config field onlyRequireEvvChangeReasonForSubmittedChanges on payorAggregatorConfiguration schema - opt-in smart EVV change reason detection
EVV change reason flows span 5+ editing surfaces: Visit Edit Form, EVV Panel, Check-In/Out Modal, Smart Bookings, Mobile APIs - changes to these are Extra Large blast radius

EVV aggregator validation_failed messages store stub payloads (debug-only fields, no ProviderID or Sandata structure) — re-submitting them sends incomplete data to Sandata. The correct recovery path is Regenerate, which rebuilds from current DB data.

queueVisit() guard ordering: missing client/caregiver checked first (creates outbox record), then clientIdentifier, then employeeId, then providerMedicaidId (new — skips without outbox record since no OrganizationProvider changestream exists for auto-recovery)
OrganizationProvider.medicaidId being null is an edge case (field is required for Medicaid type) — typically caused by deleted/archived provider or stale aggregator config reference
The EVV aggregator uses defense-in-depth pattern: UI disabling (client) + server-side 409 guard (controller) + queue-time validation (service layer)
EVV aggregator resubmitMessage() follows the same supersede pattern as acknowledgeException() — atomically mark old as SUPERSEDED, create new PENDING copy, handle E11000 duplicate key with rollback

The two-step statusHistory patching pattern (push with null, then patch with positional $) is used when the pre-update value isn't available in the atomic findOneAndUpdate — works for single-user admin operations but has a theoretical race condition
Client-side disable guards with tooltips on menu items use isDisabled prop + tooltipText prop on StandardMenuItem component
RESETTABLE_STATUSES (rejected, failed, validation_failed) and ACTIVE_STATUSES are defined in shared-const EvvAggregatorConst

RCM scoped logging pattern: withScope() returns async methods. Use `await` in async contexts, `void` in sync contexts. Error classes (PortalError, ModelItemNotFoundError, etc.) and sendErrorResponse are on the base logger, not the scoped logger.
shared-const/src/logging.constants.js is where LOG_SCOPE_KEYS and LOG_SCOPE_GROUPS are defined. New modules add keys + a group entry, and the OrganizationConfig UI auto-discovers them.

Compliance module has 4 logging scopes: compliance:cims (computation/expiry), compliance:listeners (changestreams for cg/client/forms/geo), compliance:checklist (report API, Redis, sockets), compliance:jobs (agenda/workflow jobs).
E2E flaky fix pattern: prefer data-q selectors over getByRole for menu items — role-based selectors can be unreliable when menus render dynamically
E2E flaky fix pattern: wrap popover content assertions in toPass() retry blocks even after waitForPopoverContentLoaded() — sub-sections may render asynchronously
E2E flaky fix pattern: for deep linking tests, always re-navigate with full URL params instead of conditionally checking if params were consumed — simpler and more deterministic
PR #27544 is a continuation of #27498 which fixed ~30 server + client test flakes — this round targets 3 remaining E2E timing issues

PR #27336 introduces a LangGraph-based AI agent workflow pattern for document processing: convertToImages → extractAuthData → mapProcedureCodes → buildConstraintGroups. Each node is in its own file with its own spec file — good pattern for testable AI pipelines.

AWS Bedrock integration uses lazy-loaded singleton client with ConverseCommand API. Uses retry with exponential backoff + jitter for ThrottlingException, ServiceUnavailableException, InternalServerException.
Authorization import feature uses double feature flag gating (AUTHORIZATION_PANEL_V2 + AI_AUTHORIZATION_IMPORT) plus permission gating (ai-authorizationImport) — good safety pattern for AI features.

The client.docs.utils.js docAttachmentName was changed from doc.t (document type) to filename (doc.name || doc.data.n || doc.t) — this is an ungated behavioral change that affects all document attachments, not just AI-imported ones.
Promise.allSettled is used for parallel file processing on the client side, with per-file error handling — good pattern for batch AI operations where partial success is acceptable.

EVV aggregator has two shouldQueueVisit enforcement points historically - one in changestream and one in utils. PR #27543 consolidated them into utils only, which is the correct single-enforcement-point pattern.

The AUDIT_RULE_KEYS_THAT_WILL_NOT_BE_IGNORED_FOR_CANCELLED_BOOKINGS list in shared-const/src/bookingAudit.constants.js controls which audit triggers still evaluate for canceled bookings - any trigger NOT in this list is silently skipped for canceled visits via ignoreTriggersForCanceledBooking() in trigger.utils.js.

When reviewing EVV aggregator changes, always check the queueTrigger default value - it determines whether visits queue on completion or after audit approval, and a default change affects all aggregator configs that don't explicitly set it.

When a shared utility function (like generateTimesheetPdf) is modified in a large PR (like RCM V2 #24871), both legacy and new callers need to be checked for compatibility — the template file must exist on ALL deployments, not just the ones using the new feature
The RCM V2 employee.service.js already converts to legacy format via buildLegacyPaystub() before calling generateTimesheetPdf(), so the shared function can safely use the legacy template
generateTimesheetPdfHtml() and TIMESHEET_PDF_TEMPLATE in email/index.js are now dead code after this revert — potential cleanup candidate

Compliance item `inclusionRequirements` entries have a `comp` field that stores MongoDB comparator operators like `$in`, `$nin`, `$eq`, `$ne` — this field determines whether a filter is inclusive or exclusive

The `buildFilterMismatchDetailsForPopover` function in `complianceItemModelStatus.filterCriteria.utils.js` builds the data for the N/A filter criteria popover section — it resolves reason codes to human-readable labels and values

ComplianceItemPopoverBody has two filter criteria display sections: one for 'Applicable (Filter Criteria)' and one for 'Not Applicable (Filter Criteria)' — only the N/A section shows required/profileHas details
The filterCriteria.utils.spec.js has 24 tests but none test the `isExclusive` path — this is a test coverage gap worth noting in reviews

server/templates/ is a Grunt-built directory (gitignored) generated from server/templates-src/. The ./templates/ relative path pattern is the standard way to reference built templates at runtime (used by getTemplateFileBasedOnLocale and invoice generation).

When RCM V2 rebuilds modify shared utility functions (like generateTimesheetPdf), the pattern should be to create a new dedicated function rather than modifying the shared one, since release branches may not have the new dependencies.
generateTimesheetPdfHtml in email/index.js was dead code with zero callers after the RCM V2 rebuild moved the PDF generation logic into pdf/index.js.

ComplianceItemDetailPanel uses useAttributesForSelectingOrFiltering for categoryOptions which returns undefined while loading - eagerly setting state from props before async data loads causes ReactSelect crashes
Codebase convention for const-immutable/no-mutation lint rule: use let instead of const when .current or properties will be mutated (e.g. useRef, object property assignment)
The compliance config panel has a complex section numbering system via useMemo that includes isCCTM checks for client/caregiver applicability sections
PR #27553 introduces a pattern for admin-toggleable UI labels via OrganizationConfig boolean flags + stripBetaLabel utility. Future beta labels should follow this pattern.
The Lead profile reuses Client profile routes/containers for Schedule Planner - changes to ClientRecurringScheduleContainer automatically cover the Lead profile too.
stripBetaLabel utility at client/utils/stripBetaLabel.js uses case-insensitive regex to remove ' (Beta)' suffix - available for reuse across the codebase.

Org settings pages follow a Container/Display/Panel pattern with corresponding entries in orgSettings.pages.js (routes, titles, icons, nav order) and orgSettings.constants.copy.js (field labels/tooltips).

Data import value resolution flow: CSV → server parsing (linkedEntities.js/attributes.js) → MongoDB lookup → candidates with {id, label, subTitle} → stored in ImportSession → client ValueResolutionPanel renders with ReactSelect

HANDLED_LINKED_ENTITY_TYPES coverage test pattern: a Set of all handled types + a FALLBACK_ONLY_TYPES set, with a test asserting every supported subtype falls into one or the other — prevents unhandled entity types from slipping through
Client test files for Jest should use .test.js extension (not .spec.js which is for server Mocha tests)

buildLinkedEntitySubTitle handles 11 entity types with type-specific contextual info: ADMIN_USER (role+city), ROLE (userRoles labels), CLIENT (status+city), CAREGIVER (hiredState+city), GEO (state), PAYOR (payorType), HCP (specialty+city), REFERRER/REFERRER_ORG (email), CAREGIVER_TASK/PRESET (truncated description)
joinText from shared-utils filters falsy values before joining with separator — useful for building subtitles where some fields may be missing
Data import alias mapping: `buildAliasMap.js:addAlias()` builds a normalized alias map inside `useMemo()` in ImportMappingPanel. Uncaught errors there crash the entire panel with no error boundary.
Hidden fields (`isHiddenFromMapping: true`) are used for root address configs and mirror field targets — they should never register aliases since they're not selectable in the mapping UI.

Custom fields are dynamically generated from user input and can easily collide with built-in field aliases. The alias map is a convenience for auto-mapping CSV headers; conflicts should degrade gracefully, not crash.
The `targetFields` array in `buildAliasMap` is ordered with built-in fields first, so a 'first-registered wins' strategy naturally gives priority to built-ins over custom fields.
PageContentHeaderTitle is a high-blast-radius component used in 37+ files / ~120 occurrences across the app via PageContentHeader. Any CSS changes to it warrant broad spot-checking.

In Chakra Flex, alignItems='flex-start' on a column direction Flex prevents children from respecting the parent's width constraint, breaking overflow: hidden / text-overflow: ellipsis on inner elements. The fix is to use the default 'stretch' instead.

GitHub MCP tool may return 404 / auth errors for mavencare/webplatform — fall back to gh CLI. For review comments with complex markdown, write to a temp file and use --body-file to avoid shell quoting issues.
PR #27505 introduced geo descendant expansion for pay groups which was incorrect — the correct behavior is exact geo match for caregiver selection and no geo filter on visit/booking queries
When reviewing payroll PRs, always verify whether buildBookingQueryForPayPeriod callers (bulkGeneratePaystubs.worker.js and retro/changeProcessor.js) are affected by parameter changes
Panel geoIds filter should narrow caregiver selection (by querying Caregiver.gid), not visit/booking selection — this is a key architectural distinction in the payroll pipeline

Authorization import uses source.sid field (already in ClientAuthorizationHoursSchema) for sheet grouping. The auto-generation guard at authorization/index.js:52-55 handles both user-provided and auto-generated SIDs with a simple falsy check.

Data import field additions follow a 2-file pattern: 1) Add FIELD_CONFIG entry in shared-const/modelFieldConfigs, 2) Wire into FIELDS_TO_INCLUDE in shared-utils/importViewConfigs. No handler changes needed if the schema field already exists.
PR #27585 by Max Collie is an ideal example of a minimal-blast-radius config-only feature - 9 production lines leveraging existing schema and handler logic.

memory: PR #27203 grew across 3 review cycles from a 4-file fix to a 17-file feature PR spanning 3 JIRA tickets. When re-reviewing expanding PRs, always diff the commit history against what was reviewed last time to identify new scope.

The alias-vs-name schema confusion was a red herring across two reviews. The model always had `name`; the client was sending `alias`. Checking the actual model schema first would have caught this in Review #1.

Defense-in-depth pattern: client-side UUID cleanup (cleanCalculatedFieldFormulas) + server-side normalization (remapCalculatedFieldIds) is a solid pattern for handling client-generated temporary IDs that need to become Mongoose ObjectIds.
PR re-reviews should verify code fixes by reading the actual diff, not just trusting commit messages
The MCP GitHub tool may fail with auth errors - fall back to gh CLI API calls which work reliably
When checking if previous review feedback was addressed, also check issue comments (not just review comments) for author responses

Re-review workflow: Check commit history between initial review and re-review to verify specific fixes were applied — grep the actual file content to confirm rather than trusting commit messages alone
PR #27323 pattern: .filter(Boolean) is a common footgun when arrays contain valid 0/false values — always use .filter((d) => d != null) for numeric arrays where 0 is valid
Batch create pattern uses useBatchEntryPayload as a safety layer wrapping existing formatVisitForSave/formatDataForBookingSet — good derisking approach for new features
PR #27198 expanded significantly after initial review (per-record actions, activateAccount, config unification) — re-reviews should carefully compare full diff scope vs original review scope
Config-driven action derivation pattern (actionConditionValue on option configs) is an elegant way to keep action/option metadata in sync without duplication

Server-side permission enforcement should match client-side filtering — getSessionActionConfigsForEntity (unfiltered) vs getFilteredSessionActionConfigs (filtered) creates a latent gap when future configs add permissionsRequired
actionHistory cap of 20 shared between session-level and per-record entries can cause eviction issues if per-record actions are used extensively

When reviewing PRs for geofence/GPS changes, verify claims about production vs test-only code by searching the actual diff rather than relying on file names alone. In PR #27325, checkoutRequirements.geoFenceDistanceInMiles appeared in E2E test setup only, not in any production code path.

The EVV Panel GPS suggestion flow uses a fromSuggestion flag pattern: set in ApprovedTimesSection on pill click, detected and stripped in EvvPanel.handleFormChange, with approvedFromSuggestion state tracking the latest origin independently per start/end field. This prevents cross-field contamination (e.g., end suggestion click clearing start label).

The server-side evv.utils.js has a gap where if checkInTimeActuallyChanged is false, manualCheckInOut is skipped — but GPS suggestion coords still need to be persisted. PR #27325 adds a conditional path for this narrow case.
PR #27049 bundled production changestream changes with test-only PR - always check non-test file diffs even when PR title says 'test suite'
When re-reviewing, trace each original feedback item to specific commits/lines to confirm resolution rather than trusting commit messages alone
Integration test afterEach blocks using broad deleteMany({aggregatorId: 'sandata-mo'}) is a recurring pattern - may need a shared cleanup helper with proper scoping
setTimeout sleeps in E2E tests for changestream debounce settling is an accepted pattern when commented, but a polling helper would be more robust

PR #26926 re-review: When a PR reverts a feature (DEV-44436 tolerance) and changes architecture (Call preservation vs override), the re-review should clearly map which previous feedback items are now moot vs still applicable
SANDATA EVV spec V13.0 requires 'at least one original call in or call out must be sent' - preserving original EVV capture data in Call segments is more spec-compliant than overriding them to Manual
PA VisitChanges must be wrapped in an array [visitChanges] to match MO format and SANDATA spec - inconsistent formats between state mappers is a common source of bugs
The checkIn fallback chain must include both .time and .t fields (visit.checkIn?.time || visit.checkIn?.t) since different code paths use different field names for the same data

PR #26960 re-review pattern: Author (latagore) responded thoroughly to all 5 review items with a single commit (38cda8de) and a detailed comment mapping each fix to the original issue. This made re-review very efficient.

AngularJS custom directives like mclockpicker and selectize don't expose ng-blur hooks, so blur-based validation can't be universally applied to all form question types — this is a known platform limitation.
CSS content shift prevention: when adding a colored left border to some elements, apply transparent border of the same width to ALL elements in the same context to prevent layout shift.
PR #27198 has had 3 review rounds - initial review, re-review #1, and now re-review #2. All previous feedback has been iteratively addressed by the author.

The author (maxcollie-mavencare) proactively addressed non-blocking recommendations from reviews - server-side permission enforcement was flagged as non-blocking but was implemented anyway, which is good practice.
Data import session actions use an executor registry pattern with config-driven action derivation from option configs - extensible architecture for future actions.
When posting long PR review comments via gh api, use a temp file approach (cat file into variable) rather than heredoc in the -f body= parameter to avoid bash escaping issues.

PR #27428: DAY custom fields in import config were mapped as type:DATE instead of type:STRING, causing normalizeDate() to store ISODate objects. The DATE_PICKER_STRING subType check was unreachable because the mapper dispatches on type:DATE before reaching case STRING. Fix was changing type to STRING.

When re-reviewing PRs after new commits, compare the reviewed commit hash against the latest to identify what changed since the original review. The original review was on commit beb2506a but 4 more commits were added.

Custom field value formatting in the edit panel (formatExistingCustomFieldValue) must return the correct type for each field's React component - ReactDatePicker needs Date objects, USDateOnlyDateField needs MM/DD/YYYY strings.
When reviewing function signatures for dead code, always verify against the actual file on master — the diff context may not show the full signature if it wasn't changed by the PR
The EVV aggregator queueEntityIfChanged now always supersedes pending messages on payload change (never updates in-place) for audit trail compliance — this is the canonical pattern going forward
updateAcknowledgment queries by sandataTransactionId only with no status filter — this is pre-existing behavior that may need a separate cleanup ticket

PR #27405 re-review: The payPeriodStart/payPeriodEnd keys were dead code never stored on bulkTransaction.filter documents — only startDate/endDate (paystub batches via payroll.generate.js) and start/end (invoice batches via generate.js) are real formats
BulkTransactionTagSelect.getFilterSummary() is the function responsible for formatting batch chip labels — it uses a fallback chain for date keys
The server normalizes pay period dates in payroll.generate.js:60-62 to startDate/endDate, and exceptions.service.js:333 already used the correct fallback pattern

EVV Aggregator changestream listener watches specific Booking field paths in BOOKING_FIELDS_TO_WATCH array. Changing from leaf to parent path (e.g., accountManager.approvalStatus -> accountManager) widens what change events trigger processing - this is a production behavior change even when done in a test PR.

For MongoDB changestream watching, parent-path matching catches both individual field updates AND full sub-object replacements ($set on the whole object), which leaf-path watching misses. This is relevant when code uses both granular updates and full object replacements.
Pattern: when a test PR requires production code changes to make tests pass, always flag for extraction to a separate PR for focused review. Test PRs should ideally be pure test additions.
When re-reviewing PRs, check commits after the review date to identify unreviewed new code - not just whether previous feedback was addressed
PRs by nukulb should auto-complete the hive task per task instructions
Use gh CLI when GitHub MCP tools fail with 'Not Found' for mavencare/webplatform repo
getSelfAndAllDescendantGeoIds in geo.utils always preserves original input IDs via .concat(geoIds) — this means it handles stale/missing geos safely by keeping the original IDs in the result set
When Codex flags a P1 about a custom helper, check if switching to an existing established utility resolves the concern — the established utility may already handle the edge case
PR #27505 pattern: pre-expanding geo filters into a Map<pgId, Set<string>> for resolvePayGroupForCaregiver avoids repeated expansion calls in the loop

When reviewing EVV aggregator PRs that change status enums, always check integration test files (evvAggregator.integration.spec.js, staleTransactionCleanup.integration.spec.js) which often inline their own queries rather than calling production code — these get missed easily.

The EVV aggregator previously used a fragile PENDING + sandataTransactionId compound pattern to distinguish queued vs submitted messages. After DEV-44571, SUBMITTED is an explicit status — future PRs should use status-only queries.
Changestream spec assertions on filter properties need to check for undefined (not null) when production code removes a filter field entirely.

memory: RCM V2 billing and payroll generation is NOT automatic on visit approval — it's a manual batch process triggered via queueBulkGenerateInvoices() and queueBulkGeneratePaystubs(). This is the most common reason for 'approved visit missing from billing/payroll' tickets.

Approval validation requires bookingsAudit.approvals.accountManager.approvalStatus to be exactly APPROVED or NOT_REQUIRED. REQUIRES_REAPPROVAL (set when visit is modified after approval) will cause the visit to be skipped during generation.
Key exclusion fields to check on bookings: accountingCode.data.excludeFromInvoice, accountingCode.data.excludeFromPaystub, modificationLocks.lockedForBilling, modificationLocks.lockedForPayroll
Booking model tracks generated items via invoiceV2Ids[], paystubIds[], and advancedBillInvoiceV2Ids[] arrays — empty arrays confirm no items were ever generated for the visit.

Visit modification locks: Visits with generated invoices (invoiceId/invoiceV2Ids) or finalized paystubs (paystubId/modificationLocks.lockedForPayroll) are automatically locked. The save button in VisitEditFooter.js is disabled via isSavingAllowed logic that checks visitIsLocked and visitIsInCorrectionMode.

Corrections mode workflow: Users need bookingCorrections permission to toggle corrections mode on locked visits. The flow is: click lock icon to unlock > edit > save > click lock icon to re-lock. Code in VisitEditCorrectionStatus.js calls BookingsApi.disableLocks() and BookingsApi.restoreLocks().

Key lock detection functions in shared-utils/src/bookings/bookingsLocks.js: isBookingLockedForBilling() checks lockedForBilling, invoiceId, and externalBillingSubmitDate. isBookingLockedForPayroll() checks lockedForPayroll, paystubId (v1 only, not v2 paystubIds since v2 can be DRAFT), and externalBillingSubmitDate.

Two permissions control locked visit editing: bookingCorrections (toggle corrections mode) and bookings-overrideModificationLocks (edit without corrections mode). Both defined in VisitEditFormTabPanels.js lines 147-150.

Common support pattern: 'Save Changes greyed out' tickets are almost always visits with billing/payroll items generated. Explain corrections mode workflow and check user permissions before investigating further.

Active Location Tracking feature: Controlled by feature flag mobileCaregiverVisitActiveLocationTracking (iOS) / VISIT_ACTIVE_LOCATION_TRACKING (Android) and geo-level locationTrackingV2 config. Tracks caregiver GPS every 30 seconds during visit window.

Android foreground service notification is mandatory per Google policy — the 'Tracking in Progress' notification cannot be hidden while active location tracking runs. Notification text is in android/core/common/src/main/res/values/strings.xml.
Location tracking can be disabled at 3 levels: feature flag (org-wide), geo-level (locationTrackingV2.isLocationTrackingEnabled), or per-booking (locationUpdateRequirements null = no tracking).

Office staff can view continuous caregiver location data via caregiverLocations API — requires caregiverLocations permission. If customer says they can't see location data, check this permission first.

Key files: Android VisitLocationUpdateForegroundService.kt, iOS ActiveLocationTrackingProvider.swift, server caregiver/query/locationTracking.js for config logic, caregiverLocations.controller.js for office query API.

Caregiver availability model (caregiverAvailability.schema.js) only supports weekly interval recurrence via diffInWeeks % interval === 0. No monthly Nth-weekday patterns (e.g., 3rd Saturday of month) are supported.

Key availability files: server/api/caregiver/caregiverAvailability.schema.js (schema), shared-utils/src/caregiver/availability.utils.js (recurrence logic), client/app/caregiver/profile/utils/caregiverProfile.availability.utils.js (client validation).
Feature requests already triaged as 'Referred to Ideas Forum' still benefit from internal technical analysis comments — helps dev team assess feasibility if the idea gains votes.

Caregiver termination in webplatform is a two-step process: (1) caregiver status → TERMINATED, (2) user account → DEACTIVATED. Step 2 only happens if the office user has the 'users-deactivate' permission, which controls visibility of a checkbox in the termination dialog (CaregiverPostHiredTerminalStatusPanel.js and CaregiverApplicationTerminatingPanel.js, line 51). The checkbox defaults to checked when visible.

When customers report inconsistent behavior between different office users performing the same action, the first thing to check is role permissions — many UI elements and API actions are gated by permission keys that may differ between roles.
The 'users-deactivate' permission is labeled 'Deactivate Account' in the UI under the 'Users' category in Settings → Roles & Permissions (defined in customer.roleList.utils.js line 352-356).
Caregiver user status is denormalized into caregiver.queries.user.st — if the User document isn't updated, the denormalized status will still show SIGNED_UP even after caregiver termination.

CG App Emergency Contacts visibility is controlled by org config `clinical.carePlans.showContactInfoInLegacyCarePlan` (default: true). Admin UI path: Organization Settings → Clinical → Care Plans → 'Show Contact Info in Legacy Care Plan'. When disabled, strips phone/email but preserves names/relations. Only affects careplan view — client details MobileClient projection still shows emergencyContacts separately.

Mobile CG app Environmental Conditions is a known feature gap: only 8 fields exposed (smoke, smoker, smokeInHome, pets, dogs, cats, dogsNum, catsNum) vs 51+ fields in the full client.model.js home schema. No expand/collapse UI exists. Relevant files: mobile.caregiver.client.projection.js (lines 14-70), client.model.js (lines 362-456).

Precedent for disabling careplan contact info: DEV-44123 created an upgrade script for Bayada in Feb 2026 (2026-02-26-02-09-07-647_DEV-44123_DisableCarePlanContactInfoForBayada.upgrade.js). Same pattern can be reused for other orgs.
Zoho search for ticket numbers (e.g. VHC-3697) may return empty — fallback to list_tickets with desc sort and grep/parse the results to find the numeric API ID.

The 'Join Datasets' feature in Dataset Report Builder is controlled by TWO conditions: (1) feature flag ALLOW_DATASET_REPORT_LOOKUPS must be enabled, AND (2) the selected primary dataset must be a key in DATASET_JOIN_DATASETS_MAP in shared-const/src/dataset.reports.constants.js. If either condition fails, the Join Datasets UI is completely hidden.

DATASET_JOIN_DATASETS_MAP defines which datasets can join with which others. Currently supported: Visits, Caregivers, Additional Charges, Excluded Charges, Leads, RCM V2 Paystubs/Payroll/Accrual, Client Contacts, Temporary Unavailability, Paid Time Off. Many datasets (Expenses, Invoices, Journal Lines, etc.) do NOT support joins.
The ALLOW_DATASET_REPORT_LOOKUPS feature flag was deployed via upgrade 2025-10-23-16-51-10-288 with desiredEnvs: ['ck', 'tribute']. It should be active on all CK environments running 4.1.0+.

For mileage reimbursement reporting, the recommended approach is Visits as primary dataset joined with Caregivers, or Additional Charges joined with Caregivers — since mileage data lives in visit/charge records, not in a dedicated mileage dataset.

Monthly recurring charges in webplatform are processed by recurringChargeLineItems.js — occurrence is calculated by starting from charge's dateRange.start and adding 1 month until reaching the billing service window. If the occurrence doesn't land within the service window, the charge is skipped.

Deduplication for monthly recurring charges uses a key of clientId:recurringChargeId:YYYY-MM — if a FINALIZED line item already exists for that combo, the engine skips to prevent double-billing (DEV-43348).
The 'Nutritional' charge type is not special-cased in the billing engine — it's just a recurringChargeAttribute with a text label. All monthly recurring charges follow the same billing logic.

For CK billing issues with recurring charges, the most common root causes are: (1) service window not including the occurrence date, (2) charge end-dated prematurely, (3) dedup from prior finalized run, (4) no active Private Pay plan for the client.

Viv AI Chatbot access is controlled at the Role level via two permission fields: p.ai (primary AI permission) and sub.ai.copilot (VIV AI sub-permission). Both must be true for a user to see the chatbot.
The permission string 'ai-copilot' is checked by hasPermission() in TopNav.js (frontend) and auth.hasRoleAndPermission('admin', ['ai-copilot']) on backend routes.
AI permissions were enabled for CK via upgrade scripts (2025-09-13 and 2025-10-30). Tribute Home Care may need similar role updates since it's on a different release branch (4.0.1-tribute).
For targeted AI access without affecting all users on a role, the best approach is creating a secondary role with just AI permissions and assigning it to specific users via adminRoles.other.
THC prefix in Zoho ticket numbers = Tribute Home Care department. The Zoho search API doesn't find tickets by ticket number — must use list_tickets and filter.

Editing submitted caregiver notes (forms) requires TWO conditions: (1) user must have an admin-type role (server-side isAdmin() check in formData.utils.js line 2386), and (2) the role must have `sub.forms.editForms: true` permission.

There are two distinct form editing permissions: `forms-editForms` (Edit All Forms - any submitted form) and `forms-editMyForms` (Edit My Forms - only forms you submitted). For office staff editing caregiver notes, they need `editForms` since they're editing other people's submissions.

The form editing UI is in the attached forms controller (attachedForms.controller.js). The canEditForm() function checks permissions and only shows the Edit button for submitted forms if the user has the right permission.

Secondary roles (adminRoles.other) are an effective way to grant targeted permissions to specific users without affecting all users on their primary role. This pattern works for AI access, form editing, and other permission-gated features.

Tribute Home Care tickets from Courtney Chaulk often involve enabling features/permissions for specific staff. These are typically configuration requests handled through role management, not code changes.

Expense categories in webplatform are stored as CaregiverAttribute documents with type 'additionalChargePayCategory'. They are fully admin-configurable via Admin → Attributes — no code changes needed to add new categories.

The critical toggle for making an expense category visible to caregivers is `data.showForExpenseReporting: true`. Without this, the category won't appear in the mobile app or web expense submission dropdown.

Expense categories support icons (FOOD, FUEL, MED_SUPPLIES, MISC, PARKING, etc.), rate types (Hourly, Shift, Mileage), tax treatment, payroll codes (iSolved, Paychex, Ceridian), and optional geo-filtering for franchise-specific categories.

When CK office managers ask about missing expense categories, this is almost always a configuration request — guide them to Admin → Attributes → Add Attribute → Additional Charge/Pay Category. The permission needed is `attributesV2-edit` or `attributes-edit`.

Stax (Fattmerchant) payment processor rejects PO Box addresses for ACH bank account tokenization. Physical/residential street addresses are required. This is a processor-side restriction, not a VIV code issue.

Payment method billing address validation in VIV webplatform is minimal — only checks non-empty fields (AddEditPaymentMethodsPanel.js lines 265-270). No PO Box, format, or content validation exists in VIV code.

The payment method flow is: Frontend form -> StaxJS.tokenize() client-side -> Stax API -> error returned via useStaxErrorToast hook. Errors surfaced as toast messages come from Stax's error.errors array or error.message.

Google Places API autocomplete has trouble with PO Box addresses — they lack street_number and route components, which causes getGoogleAddressComponentsFromAddress() to generate an empty addressLine1. Users should manually fill address fields when using PO Box-like addresses.

Key files for billing payment method investigations: AddEditPaymentMethodsPanel.js (frontend form+validation), useStax.js (tokenization hook), useStaxErrorToast.js (error display), paymentMethods.service.js (server-side Stax calls), stax.client.js (API connector).

The webplatform compliance system (ComplianceItemConfig) supports modelType 'Client' with source types CLIENT_DOCUMENT, FORM, COMPETENCY, and INITIAL_GRACE_PERIOD — but has no billing/payment-related source type. Adding one would require a new source type in the compliance engine.

The bulk invoice generation pipeline (bulkGenerateInvoices.worker.js) validates service windows, booking approval, authorizations, and coverage segments — but performs NO payment method validation for private pay clients. This is a confirmed gap.
Payment methods are stored via Stax integration (client.integrations.stax.customerId) and retrieved from Stax API. Payment method presence is not surfaced anywhere in compliance views.

The address validator in shared-utils/src/address.js requires street_number and route components from Google Places API, which causes PO Box addresses to fail validation. This affects payment method setup for clients using PO Box addresses.

VHC-3702 and VHC-3701 are related tickets from the same submitter (Michael Braun, Comfort Keepers) — the PO Box address validation issue in VHC-3701 compounds the billing compliance gap described in VHC-3702.

CLIENT_DOCUMENT_TYPES in shared-const/src/document.constants.js contains hardcoded system document types (Care Plan Service Agreement, CCAC Letter, AHS Letter, etc.) with permission keys. These labels are NOT configurable per-account via admin UI.

There are two separate document type systems: (1) hardcoded CLIENT_DOCUMENT_TYPES with role-based permissions, and (2) custom geo.documentTypes[] configurable via Admin → Geos → Documents. They serve different purposes but can be used together as a workaround for label customization.

To effectively 'rename' a hardcoded document type for a single franchise, the workaround is: create a custom geo document type with the desired name + remove the permission for the original hardcoded type from the franchise's roles.
The 'carePlan' permission key maps to 'documents-carePlan' in the role permission system — unchecking this hides 'Care Plan Service Agreement' from the client document type dropdown.

VIV onboarding/training videos are managed externally (not stored in the codebase or Knowledge Center). The built-in Knowledge Center feature (sidebar nav) is for admin-published articles, not VIV platform training content. Support agents need to provide external training portal links for onboarding requests.

Admin user creation in VIV: Settings → Users → Add User. Requires users-createAdmin permission (permissionKeys in customer.roleList.utils.js line 1232). The AddUserModal (addUserModal.controller.js) posts to /api/users/adduser with fn, ln, email, role, and primaryGeoId fields.
VHC-3704 type tickets (Training Requests) are configuration/guidance tasks, not code issues. The support agent's role is to provide links and walk through UI steps.
VIV-prefixed tickets are in the 'A-Viv Technologies' department (ID: 1078812000000006907) — the general/internal Viv department, not customer-specific like VHC (CK), THC (Tribute), or BYD (Bayada).

Zoho Desk phone integration auto-generates tickets for missed calls with subject 'Inbound Missed Call from (phone)' and a system comment. These have no account linked, no category, and no priority. They also auto-create contacts from the phone number.
Zoho search API does NOT find VIV-prefixed tickets by ticket number — use list_tickets sorted by createdTime desc as fallback, same pattern as BYD tickets.
Repeated missed calls from the same number create duplicate tickets (e.g., VIV-429 and VIV-430 from same caller 5 min apart). Support agents should close duplicates.

Duplicate missed call tickets from the same phone number should be quickly cross-referenced with VIV-429/430 pattern — check if the same number already has a ticket before deep-diving. Simple internal comment marking as duplicate and referencing the primary ticket is sufficient.

CRITICAL BUG FOUND: Visit changes disappear after save in Advanced Editor for recurring visits. Root cause is the booking set regeneration logic that deletes and recreates all bookings. When editing an individual visit in a recurring series at the weekly schedule level (Advanced Editor), the changes are saved but then lost if: (1) The booking set gets regenerated, which happens when time or date changes are detected on the booking set level, or (2) Another update triggers regeneration. The flow

The bug manifests because: (1) User edits individual visit in week view (e.g., changes caregiver, time, etc), (2) Frontend sends UPDATE_SINGLE for that visit, (3) Backend calls updateBooking() which unsetsthe bsid field, (4) If any booking set details or times also changed, regenNeeded=true is set, (5) _regenerateBookingSetBookings() deletes ALL future bookings and recreates them fresh from the booking set template, (6) User sees changes saved but when they come back, changes are gone (replaced

Feature flag ALLOW_RECURRING_VISIT_UPDATES_WITHOUT_REGEN_IF_POSSIBLE (line 133 in scheduling.visit.save.utils.js) exists to disable regeneration when only detail changes occur. However, even with this flag enabled, if there are time changes on the booking set, regeneration happens and overwrites individual visit edits. The logic at lines 160-169 shows regenNeeded depends on hasDateChanges OR (hasTimeChanges AND flag disabled). When regenNeeded=true, _regenerateBookingSetBookings is called which

Advanced Editor batch save for recurring visits can silently fail. The selectHaveOrphaningFormFieldsChanged selector (visitEditSelectors.js:223-235) uses stale initialFormValues when processing sequential edits of the same booking set, causing skipNonEVVVisitUpdate to be set and the DB write to be skipped. UI shows changes (optimistic update) but they vanish on reload.

Booking set regeneration (_regenerateBookingSetBookings in bookingSet.modification.utils.js:195-223) deletes ALL future bookings and recreates from template whenever date/time changes trigger regenNeeded=true. This wipes any individual visit customizations. Feature flag ALLOW_RECURRING_VISIT_UPDATES_WITHOUT_REGEN_IF_POSSIBLE mitigates for time-only changes but date changes always regenerate.

When individual visits from a booking set are edited, the system unsets bsid (bookings.modification.utils.js:62-63) to orphan the visit. But if skipNonEVVVisitUpdate is incorrectly set, the orphaning never happens and the visit remains linked to the booking set, vulnerable to regeneration overwrites.

For 'visit changes disappearing' tickets: check the bsid field first. If bsid is still present, the edit was likely skipped (never orphaned). If bsid is absent but data is wrong, regeneration overwrote the edit. This distinguishes the two failure modes.

CaregiverApplication.js handleSave() (lines 161-252) has no isLoading state, no try-catch, and doesn't disable the submit button during its 3-step async save. The SubmitButton component already supports isLoading/loadingText props via Chakra UI but they're never passed. This is the root cause of 'application spinning' and duplicate application tickets.

Caregiver duplicate detection (getDuplicateApplications in caregiver.utils.js:575-623) is admin-only post-hoc — it is NOT called during application submission. Each submit independently creates a new caregiver via POST /api/caregivers. Duplicate cleanup must be done manually by admins via the Caregivers list.

The application form submit flow is: (1) CaregiverApi.createCaregiver(), (2) loop through all form questions calling DocumentsAPI.updateFormQuestion() sequentially (can be very slow), (3) DocumentsAPI.submitForm(). Step 2 is the main bottleneck — many questions = many sequential API calls.

For CK franchise identification from Zoho tickets: use zoho_get_contact to get the contact's custom fields — cf_viv_login_url contains the franchise URL (e.g., comfortkeepers-157.vivtechnologies.com). This maps to the environments doc for release version.

Note categories in Viv are CaregiverAttribute documents with type 'activityLog' and data.isNoteCategory: true. Fully configurable via Admin → Attributes UI — no code/DB changes needed. Key files: caregiverAttribute.model.js, activityLogCategory.seed.js, attribute.constants.js, NoteCategoryTagSelect.js.

System note categories (Schedule Change, Service Exception, Client Update, Billing/Payroll) are seeded with system: true flag which hides their data fields from the admin UI. Custom categories have full UI editability including icon, color, isNoteCategory, and isTaskCategory toggles.

CK-857 contact Thomas Bormann (thomasbormann@comfortkeepers.com) is a Finance Admin who submits frequent configuration requests (also VHC-3672 QBO Sync). His Viv login URL is comfortkeepers-857.vivtechnologies.com.

BlueSummit/Ascend recurring billing uses a 4-level hierarchy: BillingRecurrence → BillingTemplate → BillingTemplateRecurrence → BillingTemplateRecurrenceAdmission. The RecurringBillingJob (AscendJobsCore/Billing/RecurringBillingJob.cs) runs daily and uses stored proc ascsp_BillingTemplateItemEffective. BillingTemplateHistory prevents duplicate billing keyed on RunMonth/RunYear/AdmissionUID.

CK-615 (Comfort Keepers NW Michigan, billing@comfortkeepersnwmi.com) uses BlueSummit/Ascend for RCM/billing. Contact Kristina Baker is a Finance Admin. When investigating billing issues for this franchise, look at the bluesummit codebase, not webplatform.

For recurring charge not billing issues in BlueSummit, check the full status chain: BillingTemplateRecurrenceAdmission.Status, BillingTemplateRecurrence.Status, BillingTemplate.Status, Client.Status, Admission.Status (all must = 1). Also check EffectiveEndDate and Admission.DischargeDate. UI path: Client → Admission Detail → Recurring Billing (under Reimbursement Rates).

Note category addition requests are a common pattern across CK franchises — VHC-3707 (CK-857) and VHC-3708 (CK-157) came in on the same day. GM (Gross Margin) on visits is denormalized at booking.queries.grossMargin and recalculated by a 5-min background job (grossMargin.agenda.js), NOT in real-time. The UI reads totalGrossMarginPercentage from the cached document. When users report stale GM, first try wait+refresh or re-save the visit.

For 1:2 visits (shared visits), the system creates two separate bookings with the FULL caregiver rate on each. It does NOT split caregiver cost across linked clients. linkedClientsSummary is stored but never used in GM/rate calculations. This means individual visit GM can go negative if caregiver rate >= client rate.

There is a known stale GM bug acknowledged in the codebase (HACK comment in bookings.externalBilling.controller.js line 317) where GM values don't always update correctly. The team force-recalculates before billing submission as a workaround.

Mobile caregiver app caching: The server correctly filters cancelled visits (canceled: {$ne: true} in bookings.caregiver.utils.js line 568), but there's no push notification or Socket.io broadcast to mobile clients when visits are cancelled. Caregivers must manually refresh (pull-to-refresh or log out/in) to see updated data.

Scheduling conflict checks are WARNING-based, not blocking. All conflict reports in scheduling.visit.warnings.utils.js are marked isBlocking: false (line 325). The ignoreDoubleBooking flag in bookingSet.controller.js (line 283) can bypass checks entirely. No database-level constraint prevents overlapping caregiver assignments.

Caregiver-to-client assignment does NOT validate application status. getCaregiverProfileForClient() in caregiver.utils.js (line 390) only checks {active: true} or {pinned: true} on connections, not whether the caregiver applied. Manual care team additions via addMember() also skip application validation.

Important: Making a client 'inactive' or 'cancelled' does NOT automatically cancel their scheduled visits. Visits must be individually cancelled. This is a common source of confusion for CK franchises reporting cancelled clients still appearing on caregiver phones.

VHC-3710 (CK-237): Missing hours on invoice due to manual clock-out error. Standard Corrections Mode workflow resolves this — unlock visit, correct time, save. Invoice auto-adjusts via change stream listener. No voiding needed unless invoice is reconciled.
